services.name: Routine House Cleaning

content.description: We clean the rooms and surfaces we agree on in your lived-in home, on the visit schedule in your estimate: dusting, kitchen and bathroom surfaces, beds, trash and floors.
included: Dusting, including high dusting from the floor, in bedrooms and living areas
Kitchen counters, sink and appliance exteriors, and the inside of the microwave
Bathrooms: toilets, sinks, showers, tubs and mirrors wiped, scrubbed or polished
Making beds and vacuuming upholstery
Emptying trash and relining bins, then vacuuming and mopping the floors
excluded: Disinfecting or sanitizing fixtures
Organizing clutter, such as toys or clothes, before cleaning
Lifting heavy objects, cleaning biohazards and deep grease scraping
Heavy grease, appliance interiors other than the microwave, and grout restoration
preparation: Tell us how we will get in: a key, a lockbox or someone at home.
Keep pets secured or away from the rooms being cleaned.
Tell us about any rooms or items to skip, and put away fragile or valuable items.
Tell us your product preferences and any allergies; we ask before using a scented product.
Clear clutter from the surfaces you want cleaned.

faqs.question: How often can visits be scheduled?
faqs.answer: Recurring schedules are available. The visit frequency is agreed in your estimate, the price of a recurring schedule holds until a new estimate, and each visit is billed after it is done.

faqs.question: Do you disinfect bathrooms?
faqs.answer: Bathroom fixtures are wiped, scrubbed or polished. Disinfecting and sanitizing are not part of this service.

faqs.question: What is not covered by routine cleaning?
faqs.answer: Heavy grease, appliance interiors other than the microwave, and grout restoration are deep-cleaning work. We also don't lift heavy objects or clean biohazards.

faqs.question: Do I need to be home?
faqs.answer: You don't have to be. Choose how we get in—a key, a lockbox or someone at home—and we use that for your visits.

product.text: For surfaces with special finishes, such as natural stone or wood, follow the manufacturer's guidance for their care.

flags.text: Whether neglected or first-time homes start with Deep Cleaning is an owner decision (Q-04-06).
The 25 lb lifting limit is in the draft agreement only; the page states no weight.

services.source: guide 6.2; vault 04-service-registry CL-01; spec section 17 CL-01; Standard Of Operations/sop Routine Cleaning Checklist.md; Main Plans/Cleaning Business.md

services.name: Deep Cleaning

content.description: We do a one-time, detailed clean of your lived-in home, including the hard-to-reach areas, appliance interiors and bathroom grout that your estimate lists.
included: Dusting of high areas and trim that can be reached without a ladder
Interior window glass and, where your estimate includes them, blinds
Kitchen cleaning, with the oven and refrigerator interiors where your estimate includes them
Scrubbing bathroom tile and grout
Furniture surfaces, living areas and floors
excluded: Ceiling fans, full wall washing and exterior window glass
Tasks that need a ladder or step stool
Vent openings, ducts and range-hood fans
Restoration of damaged surfaces
preparation: Clear toys, clothes and clutter from floors and counters before we arrive.
Make sure the water, electricity and heating or cooling are on.
If your estimate includes the refrigerator interior, empty it or tell us how to handle the food.
Put away fragile and valuable items, and tell us what furniture may be moved.
Tell us about sensitive surfaces, such as natural stone, coated glass, leather or wood furniture.
Keep children and pets away from the rooms being cleaned.

faqs.question: Are the oven and refrigerator interiors included?
faqs.answer: Only when your estimate lists them. Written scope and price for your approval.

faqs.question: Do you move appliances?
faqs.answer: No. We don't pull out the stove or refrigerator.

faqs.question: How is deep cleaning different from routine cleaning?
faqs.answer: Deep cleaning is a one-time, detailed clean that can include appliance interiors and grout scrubbing. Routine House Cleaning is recurring upkeep of the rooms and surfaces we agree on.

faqs.question: Do you remove mold?
faqs.answer: No. If mold is suspected, the affected work stops. We do no sampling or testing.

product.text: For natural stone, coated glass, leather and wood finishes, follow the manufacturer's guidance for their care.

flags.text: Included versus add-on is undecided for the oven, refrigerator, blinds and vanity drawers (C-CL02-01); the page says "where your estimate includes them".
The line between cosmetic mildew and mold that needs referral is not set (X-06; Q-31-10).

services.source: guide 6.2; vault 04-service-registry CL-02; spec section 17 CL-02; Standard Of Operations/sop Deep Cleaning CheckList.md; Main Plans/Cleaning Business.md

services.name: Move-In/Move-Out Cleaning

content.description: We clean an empty home before you move in or after you move out: closets and cabinets, the kitchen and bathrooms, interior windows and doors, and the floors.
included: Ceilings and corners, light fixtures and return vent covers
Closets and shelving, interior windows, and doors and frames
Kitchen cabinets and drawers, oven and range, refrigerator and freezer, countertops and sinks
Bathrooms: toilets, showers and tubs, mirrors and vanities
Floors: vacuuming along the edges and mopping
Noting existing damage separately from the cleaning
excluded: Homes that are still lived in
Removing furniture, boxes or other items left behind; we remove obvious trash only
Baseboard washing, exterior window glass, floor stripping and drain clearing
Carpet shampooing, wall washing, and garage or exterior cleaning
preparation: Have the home empty of furniture, personal items and trash bags before the visit.
Leave the electricity and water on.
Tell us how we get in, who our site contact is, and who may approve entry and payment.
Tell us how you want the refrigerator and freezer left.
Share the landlord's or lease checklist, if you have one.
Plan movers and other contractors around the cleaning visit.

faqs.question: Will this get my security deposit back?
faqs.answer: We can't promise any deposit outcome. We clean to the scope in your estimate and note existing damage separately.

faqs.question: What happens to items left in the home?
faqs.answer: We remove obvious trash. Other items left behind are not removed.

faqs.question: Can you clean while we are still living there?
faqs.answer: This service is for empty homes. For a lived-in home, see Deep Cleaning or Routine House Cleaning.

faqs.question: Are baseboards and exterior windows included?
faqs.answer: No. Baseboard washing and exterior window glass are not part of this service.

flags.text: Occupied move-outs are an open owner question (Q-04-05).
Authority to discard third-party property left behind is an attorney question (Q-30-17).

services.source: guide 6.2; vault 04-service-registry CL-03; spec section 17 CL-03; Standard Of Operations/sop Move-In and Move-Out Cleaning Checklist.md; Main Plans/Cleaning Business.md

services.name: Post-Construction Cleaning

content.description: We do the detail and final cleaning of construction dust and residue after a renovation, in passes, only in the areas every trade has finished and released.
included: Vacuuming construction dust and gathering debris, including in window tracks
Removing paint and plaster spots from glass, peeling protective film and stickers, and removing adhesive
Cleaning cabinet interiors, fixtures and hardware
A final wipe-down of walls, fixtures and floors
excluded: Floor scraping, floor buffing, vents and registers, and cabinet exteriors
Hauling away construction debris
Exterior glass
preparation: Make sure every trade—painters, floor installers, plumbers and others—has finished in the areas to be cleaned.
Keep the power on and the water running.
Tell us which areas are ready before each visit.
Tell us about any labels or stickers that must stay, and when walls and trim were last painted.
Keep occupants, children and pets out of the areas being cleaned.

faqs.question: When should post-construction cleaning be scheduled?
faqs.answer: After all trades have finished in the areas to be cleaned. We clean only areas released for cleaning, and we confirm which areas are ready before each visit.

faqs.question: Will the home be ready to move into?
faqs.answer: We clean to the standard written in your estimate. We don't state that a site is safe or ready for occupancy.

faqs.question: Do you take on builder or commercial projects?
faqs.answer: No. Residential projects only; no builder or commercial work.

faqs.question: Do you remove grout haze?
faqs.answer: We don't remove grout haze with acid.

product.text: Before washing newly painted surfaces, follow the manufacturer's guidance for the paint used.

withheldContent.topic: Work above 12 feet ("High Ceiling Scaffolding Work" in the pricing file)
withheldContent.reason: Whether it is in scope, excluded or subcontracted is an open question for the owner and the qualified safety professional (C-CL04-01).

flags.text: Metal polish and the flat mop the SOP names are not stocked (C-CL04-12).

services.source: guide 6.2; vault 04-service-registry CL-04; spec section 17 CL-04; Standard Of Operations/sop Post-Construction Cleaning Checklist.md; Main Plans/Cleaning Business.md

services.name: Airbnb Turnover

content.description: We clean and reset your short-term rental between guest stays, following your checklist: linens, cleaning, restocking, staging and photos, with damage and other exceptions reported to you.
included: A walkthrough before cleaning, with photos of any damage or heavy mess
Stripping beds, collecting towels, and starting a wash where laundry is done on site
Cleaning high-touch surfaces, refrigerator shelves and bathrooms
Making beds, restocking amenities as your checklist sets out, and staging
Floors, completion photos, and a lock-up check before we leave
Reporting damage, missing amenities, items guests left behind and urgent maintenance to you
excluded: Deep cleaning of the kitchen
Pool and hot-tub areas
Off-site laundry and linen supply
Co-hosting, property management, guest communication and buying supplies
Repairs, pest treatment and biohazard cleanup
preparation: Tell us the checkout and check-in times for each turnover.
Share your turnover checklist.
Tell us who supplies linens and towels, how many sets the property has, and whether laundry is done on site.
Tell us the restock items and levels, and where the supplies are kept.
Tell us where trash and recycling go, and your thermostat, Wi-Fi and welcome-book preferences.

faqs.question: How are turnovers scheduled?
faqs.answer: You tell us when each turnover is needed, with the checkout and check-in times.

faqs.question: What happens if guests left damage?
faqs.answer: We photograph damage we find before cleaning and report it to you, along with missing amenities, items guests left behind and urgent maintenance. We don't repair it as part of the turnover.

faqs.question: Do you do the laundry?
faqs.answer: We strip the beds, collect towels and start a wash when laundry is done on site. Off-site laundry and linen supply are not part of this service.

faqs.question: Is the property locked when you leave?
faqs.answer: Before leaving, we check that every entry door is locked and that any key or fob is back in its recorded place.

flags.text: Who supplies restock items is undecided (Q-29-13); the laundry model is undecided (C-CL05-12).
Delivery of the damage and completion photos to the host is held for privacy review (REC-002).

services.source: guide 6.2; vault 04-service-registry CL-05; spec section 17 CL-05; Standard Of Operations/sop Airbnb Cleaning and Turnover Checklist.md; Main Plans/Cleaning Business.md

services.name: Hotel-Style Housekeeping

content.description: We keep your residence on a recurring plan of visits: garment care within care labels, bed and linen presentation, light tidying and dusting, room scenting if you want it, and trash and floor care, following your privacy rules.
included: Sorting clothing left out, pressing or steaming the garments you ask for within their care labels, hanging clothes and setting out shoes
Making beds and replacing used bath linens with fresh towels
Tidying daily clutter and dusting vanity items, nightstands and dressing tables
Refreshing diffusers, misting linens and tending fresh flowers, if you want room scenting
Emptying and relining trash bins, vacuuming carpets and rugs, and damp-mopping hard floors
Leaving doors, windows, locks and the alarm as you instruct before we leave
excluded: Washing, drying and folding laundry, hand-washing delicate garments and dry-cleaning drop-offs
Cooking, childcare and pet care
Opening mail or packages
Refrigerator interiors
Deep cleaning
preparation: Tell us which rooms and items are off-limits, and what may be touched, moved or photographed.
Share your laundry, wardrobe and garment-care preferences, and which garments to press.
Point out delicate and high-value items, and which ones we may care for.
Tell us your preferred products and fragrance, and any allergies or sensitivities in your household, pets included.
Tell us the care instructions for any stone or wood floors.

faqs.question: How often are visits?
faqs.answer: Visits follow the plan agreed in your estimate. The price of a recurring schedule holds until a new estimate.

faqs.question: Do you wash and fold laundry?
faqs.answer: No. Pressing or steaming garments within their care labels is included; washing, drying and folding are not.

faqs.question: How do you respect our privacy?
faqs.answer: We follow the boundaries you set: the rooms and items that are off-limits, and what may be touched, moved or photographed.

faqs.question: What if a garment has no care label?
faqs.answer: We don't press it. We set it aside and let you know.

product.text: For stone and wood floors and other finishes, follow the manufacturer's guidance for their care.

withheld.topic: Keeping people and pets off damp floors until they are dry
withheld.reason: Slip hazard: the SOP's wet-floor control (marking the area, keeping occupants and pets off) is pending qualified review (C-CL06-02; X-11).

flags.text: Which steps each plan tier includes is an owner decision (C-CL06-V01; Q-28-21).
Who supplies hangers, towels, bed linens, diffusers and flowers is undecided (C-CL06-12).

services.name: Air Duct & Ventilation Cleaning

staffLabel.es: Limpieza de ductos de aire y ventilación

content.description: We clean the supply and return registers, grilles and duct runs listed in your estimate with negative-pressure extraction, clean residential exhaust fans, and change the filter where your estimate includes it.
included: Protecting the work area before work starts
Removing, washing and reinstalling the supply and return grilles listed in your estimate
Vacuuming the register boots and extracting dust from the duct runs in your estimate under negative pressure
Cleaning residential exhaust fans
Changing the filter where your estimate includes it
excluded: Commercial kitchen exhaust
Coil, blower and air-handler cleaning
Cutting, patching or sealing openings in ducts
Work inside attics or crawlspaces
preparation: Clear access to every register and return, and to the furnace or air handler.
Tell us your filter size, if you know it.
Tell us if anyone in your home, pets included, has breathing sensitivities.
Plan for the heating and cooling system to be off while we work.
Move or cover items near the vents.
Keep children and pets out of rooms with open registers and away from equipment and hoses.

faqs.question: Will duct cleaning improve our air quality or lower energy bills?
faqs.answer: We don't make air-quality, health or energy-saving claims. We clean the registers, grilles and duct runs in your estimate and tell you about anything we could not reach.

faqs.question: Do you clean dryer vents?
faqs.answer: This service covers home ducts and dryer vents. Your estimate lists exactly which parts are included.

faqs.question: Do you work on the furnace or air conditioner?
faqs.answer: No. We don't clean coils, blowers or the air handler, and we don't do HVAC work.

faqs.question: Do you treat mold in ducts?
faqs.answer: No. We don't do biocide fogging. If mold is suspected, the affected work stops, and we do no sampling or testing.

product.text: For filter changes, follow the manufacturer's guidance for the filter installed.

services.name: Patching & Repair

content.description: We repair localized holes, cracks and utility cut-outs in drywall walls: cutting out the damage, adding backing, patching, taping, feathering and sanding.
included: Squaring and cutting out the damaged area, adding backing, and fitting and fastening a new piece of drywall
Taping, two coats of joint compound, sanding and a light check of the finish
Wiping away dust, and priming the repair where your estimate includes it
Repairs to water-damaged drywall once the source of the water has been fixed
excluded: Texture matching and painting
Large panel replacement and ceiling repairs
Mold remediation and leak repair
preparation: Move furniture, fragile decorations and wall art away from the area to be repaired.
Keep occupants, children and pets away from the work area and its dust.
Tell us what caused the damage, and whether any leak is still active or has been repaired.
Tell us the year your home was built and about any earlier testing, if you know.

faqs.question: Will the patch be invisible?
faqs.answer: We don't promise an invisible finish. We feather and sand the repair into the surrounding wall, as your estimate describes.

faqs.question: Do you paint the repaired area?
faqs.answer: Painting and texture matching are not part of this service. For painting, see Residential Interior Painting.

faqs.question: Can you repair water damage?
faqs.answer: Yes, once the source of the water has been fixed. If a leak is still active, or mold is suspected, the work stops.

faqs.question: What other repairs does this service cover?
faqs.answer: General repairs to doors and cabinets, caulking and weatherstrip, and furniture assembly.

product.text: Before painting the repair, follow the manufacturer's guidance for the joint compound and primer used.

services.name: Texture Matching & Popcorn Removal

staffLabel.es: Igualación de textura y retiro de techo de palomitas

content.description: We remove popcorn ceiling texture in homes built in 1981 or later, then finish the ceiling smooth or with a sprayed orange-peel or knockdown texture, as your estimate specifies.
included: Masking and sealing off the room before work starts
Wetting and scraping the ceiling texture
Re-taping and re-fastening drywall seams within the repair scope of your estimate
Skim coating, sanding and priming, then a smooth finish or a sprayed orange-peel or knockdown texture
excluded: Wall texture matching and skip-trowel texture
Structural repairs, including joist cracks found after scraping
Finish painting after the primer coat
Ceilings that need platforms or scaffolding
preparation: Empty the room of furniture, electronics, clothes and personal items before the visit.
Look up the year your home was built, and tell us about any earlier testing and whether the ceiling was painted.
Plan for occupants, children and pets to stay out of the work area.
Allow access for more than one visit, since skim coats need drying time between passes.

faqs.question: Can you remove popcorn from any ceiling?
faqs.answer: We remove popcorn ceilings only in homes built in 1981 or later. If you don't know the year your home was built, please look it up before you send your request.

faqs.question: Do you test ceilings for asbestos?
faqs.answer: No. We do no sampling or testing. If asbestos, lead or mold is suspected, the affected work stops.

faqs.question: What finish do I get after removal?
faqs.answer: A smooth skim finish or a sprayed orange-peel or knockdown texture, as written in your estimate. Finish painting after the primer coat is not included.

faqs.question: Do you match wall textures?
faqs.answer: Wall texture matching is not part of this service.

faqs.question: Does it take more than one visit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Skim coats need drying time between passes, so the work takes more than one visit.

product.topic: When the new ceiling can be painted
product.text: Before painting the new ceiling finish, follow the manufacturer's guidance for the compound and primer used.

Hanging the drywall types your estimate specifies
Taping, corner bead and finishing, blended into the existing walls
Sanding, a light check of the finish, and cleanup of the work area

faqs.question: Can you move or remove a load-bearing wall?

faqs.question: What if you find damage or moisture when walls are opened?
faqs.answer: The affected work stops, and we explain what we found. No added work or price changes without your agreement.

faqs.question: Is painting included?

faqs.question: Is painting included?

faqs.question: Which walls can you hang on?

services.name: Barbecue & Grill Cleaning/Maintenance

content.description: We clean your gas grill: the grates, flavorizer bars, heat shields and other removable parts, the cookbox, the outside of the burner tubes and the exterior, within the grill manufacturer's guidance. We do no gas-component repair.
included: Shutting off the gas supply and taking out the grates, flavorizer bars, heat shields and grease trays
Soaking the removed grates and shields
Scraping the cookbox and brushing the outside of the burner tubes
Reassembling the grill and polishing the exterior
excluded: Charcoal, pellet, electric and smoker grills
Repairs to gas valves, regulators, hoses or igniters, and parts replacement
Cleaning or emptying grease trays, steam cleaning, and clearing nests from burner tubes
Rust or paint repair

services.name: Wallpaper Removal & Surface Restoration

staffLabel.es: Retiro de papel tapiz y restauración de superficies

content.description: We remove wallpaper and its adhesive after testing the removal method, wash off the residue, and skim-repair minor damage so the walls are ready for primer.
included: Protecting floors and baseboards with plastic sheeting
Testing the removal method, then scoring where appropriate, softening with an enzyme solution or steam, and lifting the paper
Removing leftover adhesive and washing the walls with clean water
Sealing minor tears in the drywall paper, skim-coating rough spots, dents and seams, and sanding
excluded: Primer and paint
Repairs beyond minor tears, and adhesive that enzyme solution and steam do not loosen
Ceiling paper and borders along the ceiling
Plaster walls, wallpaper hanging, fixture removal and furniture moving
preparation: Move furniture, wall hangings and window treatments away from the walls.
Keep children and pets away from steam, chemicals and outlets during the work.
Make sure running water is available and the room can be ventilated.
Allow access for more than one visit, since repairs need drying time.
Tell us the year your home was built, if you know it, and about any known leaks or past mold.

faqs.question: Will removing wallpaper damage my walls?
faqs.answer: Some minor tearing of the drywall paper can happen. We seal minor tears and skim-coat rough spots. No added work or price changes without your agreement.

faqs.question: Do you paint after removal?
faqs.answer: No. Primer and paint are separate. See Residential Interior Painting.

faqs.question: Do you remove wallpaper in older homes?
faqs.answer: We don't take on paint-disturbing work in homes built before 1978.

faqs.question: What if the glue won't come off?
faqs.answer: If the adhesive doesn't release with enzyme solution and steam, we stop and talk with you before trying anything else.

product.topic: When the walls can be primed or painted
product.text: Before priming or painting, follow the manufacturer's guidance for the joint compound and sealer used.
